Range Rover Autobiography LWB Goes for $18K at Auction, SUV Was Over $152,000 New
16 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Were you somehow under the impression that you need to be loaded if you want to buy a modern Range Rover ? Well, you don’t, especially if you opt for the previous generation, because this one now goes for pennies on the dollar.
The L405 hasn’t aged badly at all, and the average Joe might look at it and say that it has to be new. Production spanned between 2012 and 2021, and this model was offered with several gasoline units, including a V8, and a few diesel engines. And it was a very big boy, measuring 204.7 inches (5,199 mm) in length in the LWB (long wheelbase) configuration, 87.4 inches (2,220 mm) in width, and 72.2 inches (1,835 mm) in height, and had 122.9 inches (3,122 mm) between the axles.
Pictured above is a 2016 Range Rover Autobiography AWD with a Santorini Black Metallic exterior and an Ebony / Vintage Tan leather interior. It rides on 22-inch (Style 707) wheels, has an active locking rear differential, and power running boards. It also features individual seats at the rear, a rear-seat entertainment system, heated, ventilated, and massaging seats with power adjustment, a panoramic sunroof, a Meridian sound system, and adaptive cruise control, among other stuff.
This long wheelbase luxury-oriented SUV packs a V8 engine under the hood. It is a supercharged 5.0-liter unit that develops 518 hp (525 ps/386 kW) and 461 lb-ft (625 Nm) of torque. This model took just under five and a half seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from zero when it was new, and had a 155 mph (250 kph) top speed. The output and thrust are channeled to all four wheels through an eight-speed automatic transmission.
Photo: Cars&Bids But what about the known flaws, you ask? Well, these include some corrosion on the underbody, curb rash on the wheels, and some chips on the outside. And to be honest, that is definitely not bad at all for something like this, is it? After all, we are talking about a 2016 model year machine that has been a daily driver, by the looks of it, ever since it left the dealership back in the day. And it has seen plenty of action over the years, as you are about to find out.
The 2016 Range Rover Autobiography AWD in question is said to have had its fuel system cleaned/serviced in July 2026, and that is also when the engine oil and filter were changed. The vehicle had 91,794 miles (147,728 km) then, and at the time of cataloging, the odometer read 92,600 miles (149,000 km). Thus, this is far from being a barely-driven example, but then again, you did not think it would have fewer miles under its belt, did you? After all, we are talking about a ride that sold for $18K.
Actually, the selling price was $18,609, as this SUV was listed for grabs on Cars&Bids as part of an online auction that recently ended. The gavel hit the table on October 29, 2026, and the vehicle was advertised at the excitement of no reserve. The seller represented the titled owner, who reportedly bought it in December 2018, and they haven’t revealed why they wanted this ride gone. The Range Rover in question was $152,241 new, as per the attached window sticker.
Photo: Cars&Bids To be honest, the selling price shouldn’t be a big surprise, because it is pretty much average for this model . And yes, that includes the Autobiography long wheelbase configuration, and the supercharged V8 engine. And it proves that one must not be loaded if they dream about buying one of these. But their bank account has to contain plenty of zeros, because this model is not exactly reliable, and when things go south, it can easily bankrupt its owner.
But you already knew that, didn’t you? After all, it’s not like it’s a surprise that Range Rovers aren’t reliable, is it? But then again, it is a very comfortable, spacious, luxurious, and head-turning ride. This one went with two pairs of headphones, a spare tire, one key, and the owner’s manual. And a new set of tires, apparently, as the rubber has 2026 date codes.
From $152,241, which was the original selling price, and $18,609, which was how much it fetched at the end of the online auction is a $133,632 difference, and it translates to almost $1.5 per mile in depreciation alone. Needless to say that the Range Rover is not for everyone, but if you feel like it is the ride of choice for you, then you must have deep pockets, as mentioned above.
Now, if you came across this 2016 Range Rover Supercharged Autobiography LWB and saw that it is advertised at no reserve, how much would you have paid for it knowing what we told you about it? And better yet, would you have bought it? You can check out this SUV in more detail here on the quoted website.
